review.one_sentence_verdict: A well-intentioned identification ladder whose headline operation-vs-container result (T≈R, [−5.6, 5.6]) and honest Kimi downgrades largely dissolve the paper's own contribution, leaving narrow regime-specific claims that are still under-resolved at the held-out layer.

decision_critical_concerns.problem: The strongest prospective control (R, same-information operation-matched retrieval) yields T−R = 0.0 with 90% CI [−5.6, 5.6] on 18 pre-frozen DeepSeek endpoints, and T=R=100% on three Kimi endpoints across five repeats. The manuscript's own pre-registered rule says a new callable-skill claim requires a prospectively resolved T–R residual of ≥10 points. R rules that out at the registered primary resolution. The paper concedes retrieval/context parity, yet Sections 1, 2, 7, 8 and the Contributions list still frame this as a positive finding for the bottleneck framework. The contribution therefore reduces to 'some temporal operations are binding repairs in DeepSeek C3 grounding, DeepSeek C4 grounding, and held-out EIA cutoff, and they can be carried by retrieval context as well as by callable skill state' — which is essentially a replication/clarification of prior temporal-RAG results, not a new identification contract.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: The headline identification result is null on the very question (container necessity) that motivates the ladder. If the strongest supported conclusion is 'retrieval parity for these operations,' the four-arm identification ladder has no positive scientific finding beyond what the prior temporal-retrieval literature already establishes, and the paper's contribution list overstates what was found.
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: Could move from weak_reject to weak_accept if the paper were reframed around the specific non-ceiling cells where T–N>0 and T–G>0 are jointly established, with the T–R null treated as the primary headline rather than a secondary footnote.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Section 4.3 / Appendix A.7 (G0 staging and A1/A2 sequential selection)
decision_critical_concerns.problem: G0 is admitted only after an A2 replication is run because the first 35-endpoint two-repeat tranche's 90% CI [−14.3, 2.9] exceeds the ±10-point margin and 'is deliberately not promoted.' The paper then executes a fresh A2 tranche that passes. This is exactly the kind of sequential-selection bias the G0 design was supposed to prevent: the equivalence gate was applied to a later tranche, not to the same endpoints/conditions under which the T–G0 load-bearing conclusions are then drawn. The A1 'failed' tranche is not pooled and the margin is not relaxed, but its endpoints are not the same as the cells where T–G0 is then interpreted. There is no prospective rule stating that the G0–N gate must be evaluated on the same frozen cells that will later be used for T–G0 inference.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: G0 neutrality is the linchpin of the 'operation-specific value beyond neutral extra computation' claim. If G0 was validated on a different sample than the one used for T–G0 inference, the residual is no longer a within-sample same-condition residual, and the strongest positive cells (EIA cutoff, DeepSeek grounding) inherit the validity problem.
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: A single fresh G0–N run on the exact same 18 DeepSeek load-bearing endpoints and 8 EIA held-out endpoints used for T–G0 reporting, frozen before T–G0 inspection, would either confirm or undermine the operation-specificity claim. Without it, the G0 result functions as a separate study, not a control for the load-bearing cells.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Section 5.3 / Appendix A.7 (R as same-information baseline)
decision_critical_concerns.problem: R is described as 'operation-matched retrieval/context treatment' and as a 'strongest same-information baseline, not a weaker temporal-RAG surrogate.' Concretely, R runs the same T operation source on the same candidates and adds the identical object as a retrieval operation output. This is not 'operation-matched retrieval' in the sense the temporal-RAG literature uses that term — it is the T procedure's output post-hoc pasted into the context. A genuine operation-matched retrieval baseline (e.g., a learned or heuristic time-aware retriever that uses the same evidence and cutoff/alignment signal but produces its own ranking without executing T's source) would be a much harder comparison. Because R literally contains T's output, the 0.0 T–R gap is almost a tautology on the operation-level fields it measures. The 'same-information' claim is also contestable: callable state is consumable in later turns, while in-context output is one-shot.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: If R is essentially T's output materialized in the prompt, T–R=0 is a content-equality audit dressed as a container experiment. The container question (does callable skill state add value over retrieval-style integration?) is not actually answered; it is sidestepped. This matters for every Section 6/7/8 sentence that says 'retrieval/context construction is as effective as callable skill state.'
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: A genuinely operation-matched temporal retriever (e.g., time-cutoff re-ranking of the same evidence, without executing T1) run on the same 18 endpoints would convert the T–R claim from a near-tautology into a real test. If that retriever also matches T, the conclusion is stronger; if it does not, the paper's headline should be revised accordingly.

decision_critical_concerns.claim_or_section: Sections 5.1 and 7 (TimeSage-EV replication debt and EIA post-review expansion)
decision_critical_concerns.problem: The paper explicitly says the unavailable TimeSage-EV evaluated snapshot prevents an exact rerun, and that EIA is 'informed post-review validation, not an independently preregistered confirmation.' Despite this honest disclosure, the EIA expansion is the only cell where T–N is statistically defensible (7/8 endpoint means, sign test p=0.0156), and it was added after review. The 12 pre-April/8 April–May split and T1/G1 byte-reuse is documented, but the family/scorer/harness for EIA was frozen 'before execution' of the EIA phase — which is a different and weaker preregistration than the initial replay's. The reader cannot tell whether the EIA cells were selected to fit the operation they were then used to validate, because the EIA selection rule ('structural compatibility' — recurring first-party releases, explicit publication dates, etc.) is exactly the property that makes cutoff operations likely to succeed.
decision_critical_concerns.why_it_matters: The only endpoint-level inferentially significant positive result in the paper comes from a post-review, compatibly-selected expansion. The conclusion section treats this as supporting a general 'temporal operations can be causal bottlenecks' claim, but the single positive result sits on a cell that was chosen for compatibility with the cutoff operation. Without an independent held-out domain that is not pre-selected for compatibility, the regime-specificity claim is unfalsifiable.
decision_critical_concerns.acceptance_effect_if_repaired: An additional held-out domain (e.g., BLS CPI release archive or FOMC statements) frozen before outcomes and not selected on compatibility with the cutoff operation would convert the EIA result from 'fits a compatibly-selected cell' to 'generalizes beyond selection.'

noncritical_repairs: Section 5.1 should state the EIA endpoint count, repeat count, and scorer hash explicitly in the main text (currently deferred to Appendix A), so the reader can verify the p=0.0156 sign test without leaving the body.

Section 6.1 reports T=100%/G=72%/N=100% on the DeepSeek C3 cutoff cell. The text should clarify whether the 72% is a mean over 12 endpoints or a single endpoint repeated many times, since the 28-point headline gain is otherwise ambiguous between endpoint-level and observation-level.

Appendix A.5 reports 442/442 helper invocations per arm but the source-native ledger has 2,056 rows; the mismatch is explained by arm-restricted counting but should be stated in the main text to prevent confusion.

The Kimi grounding downgrade (T–G0 = −25, T–N = 0) is mentioned in passing in Section 6.2 and Section 7 but never receives the same kind of falsifiability treatment as the DeepSeek positives; a short paragraph explaining whether this was anticipated by the pre-outcome support rule would be useful.

Section 4.3 states the callable-container claim requires 'a prospectively resolved T–R residual of at least 10 points' but Section 6.2 then reports the 90% CI [−5.6, 5.6] excludes >10 only at 90%, not at 95%; the manuscript should report both and acknowledge that 90% is the pre-registered level.
claims_to_downgrade_or_delete: Delete or downgrade the Contribution (iv) framing that R 'exposes that the measured benefit is attributable to the temporal operation rather than to callable-skill packaging.' R is not a real test of container necessity; it is a content-equality audit. The paper itself concedes retrieval parity, so this contribution is empty.

Downgrade the Abstract sentence 'The evidence supports conditional operation-level temporal bottlenecks in non-ceiling regimes, but not a material advantage for the callable skill container' to specifically cite which cells (DeepSeek C3/C4 grounding, EIA held-out cutoff) and remove the implication that this is a general identification framework.

Downgrade or remove the Conclusion sentence 'those operations should be credited only after original-agent, neutral-compute, and same-information integration controls have been made explicit' — the neutral-compute control was not validated on the same cells, and the same-information control is a near-tautology.

Remove or qualify the framing of EIA as 'informs a general transfer claim' (it does not, by the paper's own admission) and re-state it as 'a compatibly-selected cutoff-compatible validation that supports the cutoff operation in one DeepSeek regime.'
evidence_that_is_now_convincing: The DeepSeek C3-R two-arm false positive (T=100%, G=72%, N=100%) is a real and important demonstration that T-vs-G alone is insufficient; the paper's central methodological point about generic-helper degradation is well-supported by this cell and the zero-call call-rate/length/position audits.
The Kimi G0–N equivalence intervals ([−4.3, 8.7] and [−9.3, 5.0] on A2) are convincing within their respective samples and the ±10-point margin is a reasonable pre-registered choice.
The held-out EIA cutoff sign test (7/8 endpoint means positive, exact p=0.0156) is the cleanest inferential result in the paper and is correctly executed at the endpoint level.
The honest disclosure that TimeSage-EV cannot be exactly replicated and that the EIA expansion is informed post-review validation is genuinely good scientific practice and should be emulated.
review.novelty_boundary: After conceding prior work on temporal retrieval (Asai et al. 2024, Yan et al. 2024, Han et al. 2025, Wang et al. 2026a, Zhang et al. 2025, Abdallah et al. 2026, Liu et al. 2026) and reusable-skill prior work (Zhou et al. 2026, Dong et al. 2026, Wang et al. 2026b, Guan et al. 2026, Wei et al. 2026, Zheng et al. 2026, Xu et al. 2026, Pan et al. 2026), the residual novelty is the three-arm bottleneck contract itself plus the demonstration that T-vs-G can produce a false positive (the DeepSeek C3 cutoff cell). T≈R actively narrows the contribution to a methodological demonstration on a few DeepSeek/EIA cells, not a new algorithm, not a new identification framework that survives its own controls.
review.single_highest_value_next_action: Run a genuine operation-matched temporal retriever (e.g., time-cutoff re-ranking or date-aware dense retrieval on the same candidate evidence) on the 18 pre-frozen DeepSeek load-bearing endpoints and the 8 EIA held-out endpoints, in place of the current R treatment that pastes T's output into context. If this retriever also matches T (T–R_new ≈ 0), the paper can claim a real retrieval-parity result and reframe around the DeepSeek grounding/EIA cutoff positives; if it underperforms T, the paper regains a defensible callable-container claim and the contribution list stands.
